calibrated.why: same rule as the 11.11 baseline: today's forward P/E is undefined (our FY2027 operating margin is -1.4% in the base, so FY2027 operating EPS is negative; FY2027 consensus EPS -6.16, pre-report) and NBIS has no own P/E history (losses since the 2024 relisting); 22 kept = a market-average multiple held for a business still growing ~7% in 2032 (judgement, not an observed NBIS multiple). Holding a sales multiple instead is not credible for a 13%-ROIC, capital-heavy business.

notes.after_the_checks: 12.11.2026 repair pass (numbers verifier + red team; change_log.md section 'After the checks'). Three inputs moved: (1) 2027 base revenue 12,250 -> 12,000, the low end of the $12-13B outlook, later growth rates the same (2028 21,551): 2026 reaches the low end of its guide only with ~325 of non-recurring revenue (2,675 without it) and the remaining Microsoft New Jersey tranches slipped to 2Q27; (2) SBC 2% -> 3.5% of revenue in 2027, 3% in 2028, 2.5% in 2029-30, 2% after (all scenarios): Q3 SBC was 58.7 = 6.0% of revenue, about twice the recurring H1 pace, and the old 2% of 2027 revenue equalled the Q3 run-rate with no growth; (3) debt rate 6% -> 7%: the 2027 plan needs about $22-24B of net new external capital; NBIS's own secured facilities are SOFR + 2.50% (asset-backed, investment-grade contract) and Term SOFR + 2.75% rising to 3.50% (Citi, 364 days), and the part not covered by asset-backed debt costs more. First-pass files: params_pre_checks.json, result_pre_checks.json (base $75.50).
notes.base_year: FY2026 revenue 3,000 (was 3,300): 'We now expect revenue at the low end of our $3.0-3.4 billion range' (letter). Nine months 1,962.1 (fact) -> Q4 ~1,038. About $325M of Q3 revenue is non-recurring (asset-light model); it stays in 2026 revenue because the guide includes it.
notes.growth: 2027 base 12,000 (was 11,500 on 11.11; 12,250 in the first pass): first company outlook '$12-13 billion', called conservative by management; the base sits at the low end because the 2026 guide is met at its low end only with ~325 of non-recurring revenue and the Microsoft New Jersey tranches moved to 2Q27 (each month of slip costs about $1.0-1.1B of 2027 revenue). 2028 base 21,551 = +80% (was +52% = 17,500): the 2027 outlook itself implies a December-2027 run-rate of about $17-18B (February above $7B rising through the year), so the old +52% would mean no growth at all after December 2027 while the company spends $40-45B in 2027 'sized for more than 1 GW of new capacity' and expects 'more than 1 GW of new capacity each year'; 21,551 = that exit run-rate plus about 80% of the 2027 pace of additions (first pass 22,000 on 12,250). 17.5B = no growth after December 2027 on a linear ramp (derived; the December run-rate is $15.5-18.5B depending on the shape of the ramp), ceiling ~33B (the guided capex fully in service at 0.47). 2029-2032 growth RATES unchanged from the baseline (+26/+16/+10/+7%), so the LEVELS are 23% above the 11.11 path (2032: 36.9B against 30.0B); the report gives no number after 2027 except 'more than 1 GW of new capacity each year' and RPO of $38.7B (+3% q/q), so this lift is judgement and carries about $20 of the base value (old levels one year early: see change_log.md). Bull 13,000 (top of the outlook; the record gives no reason for a beat above it), 2028 28,000, then the baseline bull rates. Bear 9,500 (outlook missed by ~24%: delays repeat and one tranche lapses), then the baseline bear run-off rates.

notes.conv_charges: conv = 1; charge[i] = capex - D&A - change in customer prepayments. NEW: 2027 capex at the guide, 42,500 ('$40-$45 billion, sized for more than 1 GW of new capacity'), against 11,098 in the 11.11 model. Capex above the in-service need of the year is carried as assets not yet in service and used by later growth before new cash is spent (base and bull: timing only; bear: stranded). That is why base capex is ~0.2-1.3B in 2028-2030: the 2027 spend already paid for that growth. 2026 capex 27,000 (was 22,000) sits in net cash; the extra 5,000 less the extra fleet 2027 needs is carried as prebuild. Prepayments: 2027 received at the guide 18,500 ('$17-20 billion'; bull 20,000), deferred revenue at end-2026 11,000 (9,409.2 at 30.9, fact; was 9,000), recognised over ~3 years; other years 35% of cash growth capex as before. Bull charge[0] also adds back 12834 = (Sep notes 3,270 + Mar notes 4,450 + Aug-2030 notes 3,450) x (1 + cost of equity), because in the bull these notes convert into shares.

notes.funding_note: The model funds every deficit with debt at 7% and no new shares; that mix is not the likely one (95% of the nine-month external financing was equity or equity-linked), so a $4B share sale in 2027 is shown next to the verdict (repair.py). The 2027 base cash deficit is ~22.6B after 18.5B of prepayments booked as cash (they are 'committed'; 43% of deferred revenue at 30.9 was an uncollected receivable). The only asset-backed facility closed so far is $775M (company: prepayments + asset-backed financing cover 75-85% of capex, leaving $6-11B from other sources). An equity raise instead is shown in sens.py (rows 'equity raise'). The Citi 364-day $3.5B facility matures October 2027 with no refinancing plan stated.
